sentences.text: The SFGATTA-SA scheme is an initiative by the Government of India.
It aims to provide financial assistance to small and marginal farmers.
The objective is to enhance agricultural productivity and improve the livelihoods of farmers.
The scheme offers various benefits including direct cash transfers and subsidies for agricultural inputs.
Eligibility is primarily focused on small and marginal farmers as defined by the government.
Farmers must possess valid land records to qualify for assistance.
The application process involves submitting an online application through the official portal.
Farmers may also need to provide documentation such as identity proof and land ownership details.
The timeline for disbursement of funds is typically aligned with the agricultural calendar.
The implementing authority for the scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.
State governments may also play a role in the implementation at the local level.
The scheme is part of a broader effort to support the agricultural sector in India.
